newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela six-month TEM yields fall to 24.18 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela six-month TEM yields fall to 24.18 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 468 basis points to 24.18 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.
The Central Bank said it sold 20 billion bolivars of the 179-day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills at a price of 102.08 pct. The bills carried a 28.86 percent coupon.

The bank also sold 10 billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 29.88 percent coupon at a price of 102.30 percent, and 10 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 30.93 percent coupon at an average price of 102.51 percent.
Yields on these notes fell 696 basis points to 26.20 percent for the 269-day bills, and 648 basis points to 27.71 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
At last week's auction, yields for 179-, 269-, and 358-day bills were 28.86 percent, 33.16 percent and 34.19 percent respectively.
